instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them. Chop 1/4 of the onion, mince the garlic and chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Remove the stems and seeds from the guajillos and cut them into thin strips with scissors.

Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the guajillo strips and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until they darken a shade and smell toasty. Watch them closely, they burn fast. Transfer the strips to a bowl, cover them with boiling water and leave them to soak until serving.

In the same pot, cook the onion over medium heat for about 3 minutes, until soft. Add the mushrooms and 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they darken and release their liquid.
Push the mushrooms to one side, add the garlic to the empty spot and cook for 20 seconds. Stir everything together.
Pour in the broth and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Uncover and stir in the epazote, the cilantro and the pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the cilantro wilts.
Taste it. If it's flat, add the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the drained guajillo strips. Serve with the warm corn tortillas.
method_notes: Lead is My Slice of Mexico's mushroom clear soup (caldo de hongos), which has no rating shown, so this is a fallback lead; it is the one version read that has both guajillo and epazote. Mexico in My Kitchen (3.25 from 4) and Maricruz Avalos build a similar mushroom broth with chipotle, tomato paste and squash blossoms. Vegetable broth replaces the chicken broth so the soup is vegan, and dried epazote (about 2 tsp) stands in for the fresh quarter cup, which is hard to find.
